title: Battleship: multi-cell ship placement
description:
Ships span multiple grid cells (carrier=5, battleship=4, etc.). The engine currently has no concept of a component occupying more than one cell.

## Options

### Option A: One component per cell segment
Carrier = 5 separate "carrier_segment" components placed on 5 adjacent cells. Each segment tracks damage independently. Ship is sunk when all segments are hit.
- Pro: Works with current engine (each segment is a normal component on a grid cell)
- Pro: Hit detection is just "is there a component at this cell?"
- Con: Need to track which segments belong to the same ship (component properties or naming convention)
- Con: Placement validation must ensure segments are contiguous and aligned

### Option B: Single component spanning multiple cells
Carrier = 1 component with a "cells" list: [(2,3),(2,4),(2,5),(2,6),(2,7)]
- Pro: Cleaner model — one ship is one component
- Con: Requires new engine capability (multi-cell components)
- Con: Grid model assumes one component per cell

### Recommendation
Option A (segments) — works with the existing engine. Use component properties to group segments:
```json
{"component_type": "carrier_seg", "properties": {"ship": "carrier", "segment": 0, "damaged": false}}
```
Ship is sunk when all components with {"ship": "carrier"} have {"damaged": true}.

## Placement action
PlaceShip action type already exists in ActionType enum. Needs to:
1. Accept ship type + starting cell + orientation (horizontal/vertical)
2. Compute all cells the ship occupies
3. Validate: within bounds, no overlap with existing ships
4. Create segment components on each cell

This is a server-side action (placement happens during simultaneous phase, server validates).

## Test
Place a carrier at B2 horizontal. Verify 5 segment components at B2-F2. Try to overlap with another ship — verify rejection.
close_reason: Multi-cell ship placement works via first-class engine span support (baize-jae). PlaceShip action handler validates bounds, overlap, and sets all span cells. Tests confirm horizontal/vertical placement, collision rejection, and span removal.
